blocks.text: The scale of damage to Cambodia’s 11th-century Temple of Preah Vihear has been revealed, with hundreds of locations inside the UNESCO World Heritage site reportedly hit during fighting with Thailand in 2025. Visible signs of the fighting at the temple include broken sandstone, damaged carvings, and destabilized structures, while unexploded ordnance remains a threat to conservation workers and visitors. The National Authority for Preah Vihear has conducted assessments, with verification and technical input from international experts and a UNESCO advisory panel mission, identifying hundreds of impact locations across the ancient sanctuary, raising concerns over the temple’s restoration and preservation.
